newsitem.title: USA: S&P says it will appeal Orange County ruling.
newsitem.headline: S&P says it will appeal Orange County ruling.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said Wednesday it was pleased a federal judge dismissed part of Orange County, Calif.,'s $500 million bankruptcy-related lawsuit against the rating agency, and vowed to file an appeal to have the rest of the suit thrown out.

"We were pleased that the professional negligence claim was dismissed on First Amendment grounds and we will be pursuing our legal avenues through an appeal of the remaining claim," an S&P spokesman said in a statement.
On Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Gary Taylor issued a long-awaited decision on Orange County's lawsuit against S&P.
In the ruling, Taylor said he would not dismiss the county's breach of contract claim -- its central claim.
"The county has adequately pled a breach of contract action not governed by the First Amendment's actual malice standard," Taylor said in the written decision.
The judge, on the other hand, dismissed the county's professional negligence cause of action. Taylor told county attorneys, however, that they could refile that claim.
